description.narrative:
The overall objective of the intervention is to enhance partners and other stakeholders abilities to exercise their right to freedom of expression in a responsible, inclusive and diverse manner so that they can provide citizens with reliable public interest content and information (with a specific focus on East-Jerusalem, Area C, and the Gaza Strip).
Under this overarching objective there are three outcomes (pillars):
Outcome 1: Wider media stakeholders/community are encouraged and enabled to produce ethical, inclusive and potentially viable public interest content that audiences trust and civic organisations use.
Outcome 2: Media workers of all genders are better protected online and offline and enjoy safer working environments
Outcome 3: Media support organizations advocate for laws that guarantee freedom of expression and address disinformation and hate speech.

Insatsen ska svara upp mot några av de många utmaningar media och yttrandefriheten står inför i Palestina. International Media Support (IMS) har lämnat in en ansökan till Sida om stöd till IMS Programme Strategy 2022-2024 för Palestina om 36 MSEK (12 MSEK per år 2022-2024). Programmet i Palestina är nära kopplat till IMS Menaprogram (2022-2025) vilket betyder att personal och resurser kan delas i implementeringen. Det föreslagna programmet har bedömts relevant av Sida och insatsen skulle utgöra en fortsättning av ett pågående partnerskap som bygger på tillit och ömsesidig förståelse av en vision att öka ansvarsutkrävande i Palestina över tid, genom ett stärkt civilsamhälle, oberoende media och mer professionella journalister. Insatsen kompletterar andra i portföljen inom mänskliga rättigheter-omårdet, men verkar även kompletterande till det överbryggande stödet till Palestina. IMS huvudsyfte av landstrategin för oPt (Occcupied Palestinian Territory) för 2022-2024 fokuserar på stärkande av partners och andra intressenter/aktörers möjligheter att utöva sin rätt tilll yttrandefrihet på ett ansvarsfullt, inkluderande och diversifierat sätt för att kunna förse medborgarna med påligligt innehåll och information av allmänintresse (med särskilt fokus på östra Jerusalem, område C och Gazaremsan). Under detta övergripande mål finns ett effektmål (impact objective): - Tillgång till innehåll av allmänintresse publiceras av pålitlig media som täcker, sociala, politiska och kulturella ämnen och som verkar för ansvarstagande och ansvarskrävande och människors möjligheter att utöva sina mänskliga rättigheter. Tre resultat: Resultat 1: Större delen av media intressenter/samhället är stärkta och ges möjlighet att producera etiskt, inkluderande och potentiellt livskraftigt innehåll av allmänintresse som publiken litar på och som civilsamhällesorganisationer använder. Resultat 2: Journalisters säkerhet online ökar och deras rättigheter är skyddade i domstol och genom dokumentation av brott mot pressfriheten. Resultat 3: Media stödjer organisationer och civilsamhällesorganisationer lobbar framgångsrikt för lagar som garanerar yttrandefriheten och adresserar desinformation och hatpropaganda.

To respond to some of the many challenges to media and freedom of expression in Palestine. International Media Support (IMS) has submitted a proposal to Sida to fund the IMS programme Strategy 2022-2024 for the Occupied Palestinian Territory with 36 MSEK (12m SEK annually 2022-2024). The Palestine programme is closely linked to the IMS Mena programme (2022-2025) which means it draws on staff and resources for implementation. The proposed programme has been assessed by Sida as relevant and the contribution would be a continuation of an ongoing partnership which is built upon trust and mutual understanding of a long-term vision to enhance accountability in Palestine through an enhanced civil society, independent media and more professional journalists. It is complementary to other contributions in the portfolio within the field of human rights, but also complementary to the overall support to Palestine.
IMS’ main objective of the oPt country strategy for 2022-2024 is focused on enhancing partners’ and other stakeholders’ abilities to exercise their right to freedom of expression in a responsible, inclusive and diverse manner so that they can provide citizens with reliable public interest content and information (with a specific focus on East-Jerusalem, Area C, and the Gaza Strip). Under this overarching objective there is an impact objective: -Access to public interest content published by trusted media which covers social, political and cultural issues and which pushes for accountability and the ability of people to exercise their human rights. and three outcomes: Outcome 1: Wider media stakeholder/community are encouraged and enabled to produce ethical, inclusive and potentially viable public interest content that audiences trust and civic organisations use. Outcome 2: Journalists are safer online and have their rights protected in court and through documentation of press freedom violations. Outcome 3: Media support organizations and CO advocate successfully for laws that guarantee FoE and address disinformation and hate speech.

title.narrative: Decision on Contribution International Media Support 2022-2024

description.narrative:
The IMS Palestine Programme made progress across its three main pillars: (1) supporting public interest media that produce factual, ethical, and inclusive content; (2) strengthening the safety and wellbeing of journalists; and (3) fostering an enabling environment for freedom of expression and digital rights.
This period, however, was marked by extraordinarily difficult conditions. Since October 2023, the war on Gaza has created a humanitarian catastrophe and one of the most dangerous environments for journalists in modern history. Despite immense challenges, including massive destruction, targeted attacks on journalists, and a six-month funding freeze by Sweden, IMS partners sustained operations, and adapted their programming, to ensure that Palestinian voices continued to be heard.
Under the first outcome on public interest content, partners continued to produce high-quality, gender-sensitive content (produced over 4,200 pieces) across digital and traditional platforms. Filastiniyat expanded its women-led reporting through the Nawa platform, producing over 900 media reports and multimedia stories, and leading the #GazaSpeaksUp campaign, which played a vital role in amplifying voices from Gaza, through sharing civilians testimonies translated globally and viewed by over 240 million people. Filastiniyat also strengthened coordination with local organisations to support women journalists displaced or injured during the war and documented dozens of field testimonies that have contributed to international awareness of the humanitarian crisis Wattan TV maintained its position as a key source of public interest media, producing 180 stories focusing on women, youth, and marginalized groups and launching Voices from Gaza initiative, which documented over 300 stories highlighting the struggles of women, children, and people with disabilities during the war. CDMC (Community Development Media Centre) in Gazaadapted quickly to the crisis, shifting from training to emergency response, producing six documentary films on womens leadership during the war and conducting psychosocial support and digital safety trainings for over 375 youth and women. CDMC also trained a new cohort of 25 young journalists on ethical reporting during emergencies and provided digital literacy sessions in Khan Younis and Rafah. Yura/Untold Palestine and Witness continued to amplify Palestinian visual storytelling globally to keep Palestinian narrative alive, through producing 260 visual stories, hosting exhibitions in Berlin, Amman, and Ramallah, and mentoring young journalists in refugee camps through From the Camp initiative, which published 160 stories from refugee communities. In 2024, Yura further expanded international visibility by partnering with cultural institutions in Buenos Aires and Paris to showcase Palestinian photographers work. Filmlab Palestine advanced independent film production and capacity development, completing six film productions, hosting the 2024 Palestine Cinema Days festival with 78 screenings across 17 locations in Palestine and 57 countries worldwide and piloting a new Women in Cinema mentorship programme supporting emerging female filmmakers.
Under the safety of journalists component, IMS and partners shifted their focus from planned training to emergency response. Filastiniyat played a key role in coordinating with other Palestinian organisations, including human rights and womens rights groups, to deliver a unified response. By 2024, this coordinated effort was formalised into a media task force coordinated a media task force which streamlined resources and support for journalists, including cash assistance and safe workspaces for 869 journalists most of them women (527 women). CDMC provided psychosocial support, dignity kits, and training to help journalists cope with trauma and digital threats, while 7amleh published a digital security manual, established an emergency help desk supporting journalists and human rights defenders under digital attack, and documented thousands of online rights violations. 7amleh also updated its Digital Security Emergency Manual and expanded its Arabic-language resources, responding to the rising need for protection against hacking, surveillance, and online harassment. IMS also provided new partner Mnemonics Palestine staff with mental health and wellbeing support to help mitigate the trauma of constant exposure to digital content depicting atrocity crimes.
In terms of the enabling environment and digital rights, the programme helped safeguard freedom of expression in an increasingly restrictive landscape. 7amleh continued to lead digital rights advocacy, holding tech companies accountable for biased content moderation and documenting thousands of cases of online censorship. Earlier in the programme in 2022, joint advocacy efforts by 7amleh, MADA, Wattan, and Filastiniyat successfully pushed the Palestinian cabinet to freeze a draft media law that threatened press freedom, a key policy win for press freedom.
Despite severe constraints, partners achieved substantial reach and influence. Collectively, their digital engagement spanned hundreds of millions of views, with Filastiniyat, Wattan, and Yura achieving significant global followings. While expected outcomes on ethical and inclusive journalism, safety mechanisms, and advocacy were achieved, unexpected yet vital results included the creation of emergency coordination mechanisms for journalists, global solidarity campaigns amplifying Palestinian narratives, and the use of digital storytelling as a humanitarian lifeline under siege.
Overall, the programme demonstrated exceptional resilience and adaptability, sustaining public interest journalism and digital rights advocacy amid near-total information blackouts. These results underscore IMS partners critical role in preserving the integrity of media and amplifying Palestinian voices in one of the most repressive environments in modern history.
